name: Religion and theology
question: What does religion and theology establish about this subject, divided by its key line?
scqa_question: Which single partition places every religious claim exactly once, without merging the warrant of study with the warrant of faith?
look_for: RE.O.A1 The ultimate and the human condition
RE.O.A2 Authoritative text
RE.O.A3 Practice
RE.O.A4 Community and institution
find_out: Systematise and argue (M1 Represent, M2 Derive)
rules_of_thumb: the principle of charity toward the tradition
"nobody is a Hindu in general" (study the local form first)
lex orandi, lex credendi (in ·T: worship shows belief).
collisions: Place by the subject of the sentence (the ultimate, the text, the practice, the community), then by mode.
·S and ·T are never merged. The same sentence, asserted as true within a tradition, is ·T. Reported as held, it is ·S.
An argument from premises any reasoner may grant (cosmological, ontological, problem of evil) is PL. The same argument from scripture is RE ·T.
The dated event of a tradition's past is HI, cited by RE ·S.
A civil duty arising from a religion is LA. A canon-internal duty is RE ·T.
The neural or psychological process of religious experience is MS. The discipline as practice is RE.O.A3.2.
A measurement offered as doctrine is refused. Its measurement goes to its science; the doctrine stays in ·T without the measurement's warrant.
Comparison does not inherit any canon's W13.
Māori and other Indigenous religious claims follow p2_ANZSRC45.md and need Māori-led review.
Pilot repair (claim 19). A dated event in a text's history (when the Mishnah was redacted) is HI.O.A1. RE.O.A2.2 keeps claims about the transmitted text as text: variants, recensions and readings.
Pilot repair (claim 46). Reporting what a theologian held is RE·S. Evaluating an argument whose premises any reasoner may grant is PL, even when a theologian made it.
philosophy of religion from shared premises → PL
psychology and neuroscience of religion → MS
dated events of religious history → HI
legal status of religion, religious freedom → LA
sacred art as making and form → AR
tradition-internal Indigenous knowledge outside religion → IK
open: Io's pre-contact antiquity; the axial age; the order canon-before-composition; acts addressed to two recipients; the place of tikanga (RE, IK or LA).

name: The ultimate and the human condition
question: Which doctrinal questions are distinct?
look_for: The Trinity, defined at Nicaea (325) and Constantinople (381). As true: ·T. Its conciliar history: ·S.
Tawḥīd and the divine attributes. Ashʿarī, Māturīdī and Muʿtazilī answers differ.
Createdness of the Qurʾan and the *miḥna* (from 833, UNVERIFIED date). Muʿtazilīs held it created; Ashʿarīs uncreated.
Apophatic theology. God is known by negation. Pseudo-Dionysius (c. 500); Maimonides' negative attributes.
Nirguṇa and saguṇa Brahman. Advaita (Śaṅkara, c. 8th century) against Viśiṣṭādvaita (Rāmānuja).
Śūnyatā (Nāgārjuna, c. 2nd century) as a Madhyamaka claim. Its argument alone, from shared premises, is PL.
Ein Sof in Kabbalah.
Io as supreme being in some Māori traditions (·S). CONTESTED: its pre-contact antiquity is disputed. See T/p2_ANZSRC45.md.
Otto's numinous (*Das Heilige*, 1917, UNVERIFIED date) as a ·S theory of the sacred.
Creation ex nihilo.
Whakapapa cosmogony from Ranginui and Papatūānuku. Human descent from a named tupuna is HI.O.A1.
Tapu and noa as statuses of persons, places and things.
Karma and saṃsāra; mokṣa; nirvāṇa.
Grace and synergy. Salvation by grace alone against cooperation of grace and will.
The beatific vision.

The axial age (Jaspers, 1949: roughly 8th to 3rd centuries BCE). A ·S comparative claim (W6) of a shift toward transcendence. CONTESTED: critics find no common denominator and no clean break. Alternative home: HI.O.A2 (periodisation). Filed
find_out: Systematise and argue (M1 Represent, M2 Derive)
breaks: ·S: essentialising; ·T: heresy by the tradition's own test

name: Authoritative text
question: Which text claims are distinct?
look_for: Biblical canons. The Tanakh; Protestant, Catholic (with deuterocanonical books) and Ethiopian Orthodox canons differ in extent.
Śruti and smṛti. Heard and remembered texts in Hindu traditions.
Pāli Tipiṭaka, written down in Sri Lanka c. 1st century BCE; the Chinese and Tibetan canons.
The ʿUthmānic codex (c. 650) and the *qirāʾāt* (canonical readings).
Ḥadīth and *isnād* criticism.
Dead Sea Scrolls (found from 1947) as textual witnesses (·S).
Mishnah (c. 200 CE) and the Jerusalem and Babylonian Talmuds.
Vedic oral transmission by fixed recitation patterns.
Karakia and kōrero tuku iho as oral text, transmitted in whare wānanga. Placement subject to Māori-led review (T/p2_ANZSRC45.md).

Four senses of scripture: literal, allegorical, moral and anagogical. Origen gave the first three; Cassian added the anagogical. As a claim about how scripture means: ·T. Its use as a procedure is RE.M.B2.
Tafsīr *bi'l-maʾthūr* and *bi'l-raʾy*: by transmitted report and by reasoned opinion.
Midrash and PaRDeS.
Mīmāṃsā rules of Vedic interpretation.
find_out: Systematise and argue (M1 Represent, M2 Derive)
collisions: Pilot repair (claim 19). A dated event in a text's history (when the Mishnah was redacted) is HI.O.A1. RE.O.A2.2 keeps claims about the transmitted text as text: variants, recensions and readings.

name: Practice
question: Which practice claims are distinct?
look_for: Eucharist and sacrament.
Ṣalāt and ḥajj.
Pūjā and śrauta ritual.
Karakia in performance; pōwhiri; tangihanga. Subject to Māori-led review.
Rites of passage (van Gennep, 1909, UNVERIFIED date): separation, transition, incorporation. A ·S comparative claim.
Veneration of icons and the ruling of Nicaea II (787). The icon's form and making are AR.O.A1 and AR.O.A2.
Meditation (*śamatha*, *vipaśyanā*); yoga; dhikr. Its neural correlates are MS.O.A2.
The Rule of Benedict (c. 530); musar.
Bhakti as devotional discipline.
Fiqh rulings in *muʿāmalāt*.
Halakha in the Shulchan Aruch (printed 1565, UNVERIFIED date); dharmaśāstra.
Natural law in Aquinas (*Summa* I–II q. 94) as moral theology (·T). The same argument from shared premises is PL.O.A4.
Kashrut and halal. Filed by subject: as worship A3.1, as conduct A3.3.
Tikanga as correct practice before atua and people; manaakitanga as obligation to guests. Tikanga as part of NZ law is LA.O.A1 (*Ellis v R* [2022] NZSC 114).
find_out: Systematise and argue (M1 Represent, M2 Derive)
collisions: The neural or psychological process of religious experience is MS. The discipline as practice is RE.O.A3.2.

name: Community and institution
question: Which community claims are distinct?
look_for: Papacy and councils.
The ʿulamāʾ and the four Sunni *madhhabs*; the Twelver imamate.
The rabbinate and the *posek*.
Saṅgha and *vinaya* as the monastic community's rule. Its membership rules are filed at A4.2 by subject.
Tohunga and kaumātua; marae *kawa*, which varies by iwi and hapū. Subject to Māori-led review.
Excommunication, *ḥerem*, *takfīr*.
Orthodoxy and heresy. In ·S, insider labels are marked as reported.
Apostolic succession.
Guru-śiṣya *paramparā*; Śaṅkara's *maṭhas*.
The East–West schism (1054); the Reformation (from 1517); the Sunni–Shīʿa division after 632 (·S).
Ringatū (Te Kooti, c. 1868, UNVERIFIED date) and the Rātana Church (1925, UNVERIFIED date) as Māori Christian communities.
The "gate of ijtihād closed" thesis, rejected as history by Hallaq, "Was the Gate of Ijtihad Closed?" (*IJMES* 16, 1984) (·S).
